title: Changing a yes/no fact
idea: Facts can change. A boolean variable can be reassigned from True to False, just like a number can be updated. This reviews reassignment with a new kind of value.

exercises.prompt:
What does this print?

open_now = True
open_now = False
print(open_now)
exercises.explanation: The second line replaces the value. open_now now holds False, so that's what prints.

exercises.prompt: A variable keeps only its most recent value.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Each new assignment replaces the old value. The last one wins - this is true for numbers and booleans alike.

exercises.prompt:
What does this print?

done = False
done = True
print(done)
exercises.explanation: done starts as False, then becomes True. The newest value, True, is what prints.

exercises.prompt: A seat starts empty (taken = False), then someone sits (taken = True). Arrange to show the final fact.
exercises.explanation: Start empty (False), then taken (True), then print. The order of the facts tells the story.

exercises.prompt: A battery saver is off, then turned on. Which code matches? (final fact should be True)
exercises.explanation: Off means False, then on means True. The last assignment, True, is the final state.

exercises.prompt:
A phone was muted, now unmuted. Fill the final value:

muted = True
muted = ____
print(muted)   # shows: False
exercises.explanation: Unmuting flips the fact to False. Reassignment lets a yes/no fact change over time.

exercises.prompt: Reassigning a boolean works the same way as reassigning a number.
exercises.explanation: Yes - name = new_value replaces whatever was there, whether it's a number or a boolean.

exercises.prompt:
A quick number review - what prints?

score = 5
score = 8
print(score)
exercises.explanation: The newest value (8) wins. The same rule you just learned for booleans.

exercises.prompt:
After three updates, what prints?

visible = True
visible = False
visible = True
print(visible)
exercises.explanation: Only the last assignment matters. visible ends as True.

exercises.prompt: Why is it handy that a yes/no fact can change?
options: Because real facts change - a door opens, a task finishes
Because booleans must change every line
Because True is better than False
exercises.explanation: Programs track changing facts: a seat fills, a task completes. Reassignment lets a boolean follow the real world.
